mainTopic: Is cancelled impurity still present? The back-and-forth between רב דימי and אביי about touch versus carrying, ending with רב דימי's silence and the 'rotted impurity' suggestion.
overview: This amud asks whether impurity that was cancelled out (בטל) in a majority is still there in some way and can come back. רב דימי first brings a proof from רבי אליעזר's ruling and עולא's reason for it: a tiny cancelled bit of impurity can meet its own kind and 'wake up.' אביי answers that this case is different, because there impurity woke up impurity, while here the question is whether purity can wake up impurity. אביי then challenges the idea from a משנה about פרה אדומה ashes mixed with ordinary ashes, and רב דימי answers with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the mixture does not make impure by touch, but it does by carrying. אביי pushes back with רב חסדא's rule about נבילה mixed into שחוטה. רב דימי replies that his school follows רבי חייא's version instead. Finally אביי brings רבי חייא's own teaching that a clump of blood makes impure neither by touch nor by carrying, and רב דימי is silent. The גמרא suggests he could have said the clump is rotted impurity. That answer works for בר פדא, and the גמרא begins to ask about רבי יוחנן's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's careful way of eating the mixture
steps.stepSummary: The source being brought as proof: according to רבי אליעזר, the mixture must be eaten in ways that keep it from coming in contact with water, or split into batches smaller than an egg's volume.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, what should be done with them? They should be eaten dry or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into small doughs, as long as there is not an egg's volume in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a source that is being used as proof. רבי אליעזר lists careful ways to eat a mixture that has a tiny bit of impure produce in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these options keep the food dry, avoid ordinary water, or keep each piece too small to matter. These limits only make sense if the tiny bit of impure produce is still a concern, even though it is a small minority. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: dry (eaten without being moistened with water)
the volume of an egg, the size at which food can pass on impurity

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, what will be with them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the mixed produce from the case quoted just before, where a little impure produce got mixed into pure produce.

phrases.english: Let them be eaten dry, or roasted,
or kneaded with fruit juice,
or it should be divided into small doughs,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כְּבֵיצָה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: provided that there is not an egg-bulk in one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source quoted just before this section, as part of a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That nullified impurity can come back to life (ניעור).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's restrictions on eating the mixture.

steps.title: עולא explains: the impure part can wake up again
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the restriction is a rabbinic decree. Someone might add outside impure produce and think it is cancelled out. But the tiny cancelled impure bit already in the mixture meets its own kind and 'wakes up,' so the impure side is no longer outweighed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: What is the reason? It is a decree, in case someone brings a קב of impure non-sacred produce from somewhere else and a קב and a bit more of this mixture. He will think: I will cancel it out in the majority. But since this tiny amount of impurity is there, the type finds its own type and wakes up.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's rule. This reason is the heart of the proof that a cancelled impurity can wake up again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the person thinks the outside impure קב is cancelled out by a slightly larger amount of the mixture. But the mixture already holds a little cancelled impurity of the same kind. When that bit meets the new impure food, it comes back to life and joins it, so the impure side is no longer outweighed. This shows the original small impurity was never truly gone.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
a type found its own type (same-kind joins up)

steps.confusionAlert: What 'wakes up' is the tiny bit of impurity that was already cancelled inside the mixture. It meets the new impure קב, which is its own kind, and comes back to life. Then the impure side is no longer a minority, so the new קב is not cancelled either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main idea the rest of the section argues about: whether a cancelled impurity counts as still present.

phrases.english: And Ulla said: What is the reason?
It is a decree, lest one bring
a kav of impure non-sacred produce from another place
and a kav and a little more of this kind,
phrases.notes: 'This kind' means the mixture from רבי אליעזר's case.

phrases.english: thinking: I will cancel them out in the majority,
but since there is this tiny amount —
the type found its own type and woke up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי אליעזר's ruling. That reason is what makes it a proof.
steps.raayaObject: Cancelled impurity is considered still present and can revive.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's explanation: מצא מין את מינו וניעור.

steps.title: אביי: impurity reviving impurity is not the same as purity reviving impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. In that case the thing that wakes up the impurity is itself impure, but in our case it would be something pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If impurity wakes up impurity, does purity wake up impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רב דימי that the proof does not fit. The two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עולא's case, impure food joins other impure food, so it makes sense that it revives. In the case being discussed here, the added substance is pure. It is a big jump to say that something pure could make cancelled impurity come back.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי speaking to רב דימי.

phrases.english: If impurity revives impurity,
does purity revive impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִם טוּמְאָה עוֹרֶרֶת טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 1 and 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not deny that impurity can revive impurity.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof case involves impure food reviving impurity, while the case in question involves something pure.

steps.title: Challenge from red heifer ashes mixed with ordinary ashes
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the idea that cancelled impurity is still there. He brings a משנה about פרה אדומה ashes mixed with ordinary ashes: if most is ordinary ash, the mixture does not make anyone impure. Why not at least by carrying?
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: Valid ashes that got mixed with ordinary burnt ashes: we follow the majority to decide whether they make impure. If the majority is ordinary ashes, it does not make impure. Now if you say impurity counts as if it is still there, granted it does not make impure by touch, but it should make impure by carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the whole idea that cancelled impurity is still present. He uses a משנה that seems to say the majority completely cancels out the impure ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With touch, we can say the person probably touched the ordinary ashes, which are the majority. But when you carry the mixture, you carry everything, including the פרה אדומה ashes. If those ashes are really still there, carrying should make you impure. Yet the משנה just says the mixture does not make impure.
steps.confusionAlert: Touch and carrying are two different ways of becoming impure. The whole question depends on keeping them apart.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Valid ashes that became mixed with burnt ashes,
phrases.notes: 'Valid ashes' are the ashes of the פרה אדומה. Those ashes make the people who handle them impure.

phrases.english: we follow the majority to determine whether they make impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי רוּבָּא אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה הוּא — לָא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.english: and if the majority is burnt ashes, it does not make impure.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ: טוּמְאָה כְּמַאן דְּאִיתֵיהּ דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: And if you say impurity is considered as if it is still there,
granted that it does not make impure through touch,
let it make impure through carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof, אביי now attacks the idea itself with a source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that cancelled impurity is considered still present (טומאה כמאן דאיתיה דמי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פרה אדומה ashes were still there, carrying the whole mixture should make a person impure. The משנה says the mixture does not make impure at all.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: pure for touch, but impure for carrying
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא already explained the משנה: the mixture does not make impure by touch, but it does make impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about it: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said: It is pure in that it does not make impure by touch, but it does make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the משנה was only talking about touch. Carrying the mixture really does make a person impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'it does not make impure' as covering touch only. Since carrying does make impure, the פרה אדומה ashes are treated as still present. That is exactly what the view of 'cancelled impurity is still there' needs, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was already stated about it
pure, in the sense of not passing on impurity

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, the mixture of ashes passes on impurity by carrying but not by touch. This shows the cancelled impure ashes still count as present, so רב דימי survives this challenge. אביי attacks again in the next steps, and in step 8 רב דימי has no answer.

phrases.english: But it was stated about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה about the mixed ashes that אביי just quoted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It is pure in that it does not make impure through touch,
but it does make impure through carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the ashes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the source: the משנה's 'does not make impure' refers only to touch.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the mixture is completely pure, so the cancelled ashes would be truly gone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixture still makes impure by carrying, so the cancelled impurity is treated as present.

steps.title: אביי Quotes רב חסדא Against רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רב חסדא, who says a נבילה is fully cancelled in שחוטה. This suggests the mixture does not even make impure by carrying, which goes against רב דימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רב חסדא say: a carcass is cancelled in slaughtered meat, because a carcass can never become slaughtered meat? Fine, it doesn't make impure by touching, but it should at least make impure by carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב דימי's answer by bringing a statement of רב חסדא that seems to treat the cancelled impurity as completely gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי said cancelled impurity still makes impure by carrying. רב חסדא's rule about נבילה mixed into שחוטה sounds like full cancellation with no carrying impurity left. So אביי asks: if the impurity were still there in some way, why would רב חסדא not say it still makes impure by carrying?

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה; it makes things impure
Meat of a properly slaughtered animal; it is pure
Cancelled out, swallowed up by the majority
Carrying: another way impurity spreads, even without touching

phrases.english: But doesn't Rav Chisda say:
A carcass is cancelled in slaughtered meat,
since it is impossible for a carcass to become slaughtered meat.
Granted that it does not make impure by touching,
let it make impure by carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's answer from step 5 using a statement of רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim (in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא) that cancelled impurity still makes impure by carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא treats נבילה cancelled in שחוטה as fully cancelled, with no mention of carrying impurity remaining.

steps.title: רב דימי: We Learn It Like רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that in his place they follow רבי חייא's teaching, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explained it to mean the mixture still makes impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learn it according to רב חסדא; we learn it according to רבי חייא. רבי חייא taught: a carcass and slaughtered meat cancel each other. And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said about it: the mixture does not make impure by touch, but it does make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי deflects the challenge: רב חסדא's version is not the one his school follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of arguing with רב חסדא, רב דימי says his tradition follows a different source, the teaching of רבי חייא. That teaching was explained by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in exactly the way רב דימי said: no impurity by touch, but yes by carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: You (in your place) learn it this way
We (in our place) learn it this way
One in the other, each way

phrases.english: He said to him:
You learn it according to Rav Chisda;
we learn it according to Rabbi Chiya.
Rabbi Chiya taught:
A carcass and slaughtered meat cancel each other,
phrases.notes: Whichever is the majority cancels the other one.

phrases.english: and it was said about it,
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It is pure in that it does not make impure by touch,
but it does make impure by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן בִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן בִּדְרַבִּי חִיָּיא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different tradition: the challenger's source is not the one this school follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's view is binding, so cancelled נבילה has no carrying impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי's school follows רבי חייא's teaching, explained as: no impurity by touch, but impurity by carrying.

steps.title: The Clump of Blood: רב דימי Is Silent
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings רבי חייא's own teaching: a clump of blood from a large animal makes impure neither by touch nor by carrying. Why not by carrying? רב דימי has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about what we learned: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a large animal that expelled a clump of blood, the clump must be buried, and the animal is exempt from the firstborn law. And רבי חייא taught: it does not make impure by touch or by carrying. Why? Fine, not by touch, but it should make impure by carrying! He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks again, this time using a teaching of רבי חייא himself, the very source רב דימי relied on. רב דימי cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא treats this clump like another case where impurity is swallowed up and cancelled. By רב דימי's rule, it should still make impure by carrying. But רבי חייא says it does not make impure even by carrying, which seems to contradict רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: A large animal, like a cow
A clump of thick, hardened blood
Exempt from the firstborn law: her next offspring is not a בכור
He was silent; he had no answer

phrases.english: And what about what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is our משנה here in בכורות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A large animal that expelled a clump of blood,
this clump must be buried,
and the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.
And Rabbi Chiya taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: It does not make impure, not by touch and not by carrying.
Why?
Granted it does not make impure by touch,
let it make impure by carrying!
He was silent.
phrases.notes: רב דימי had no answer for אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב דימי relied on רבי חייא, אביי challenges him from another teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's rule that cancelled impurity still makes impure by carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא himself rules the clump of blood makes impure neither by touch nor by carrying, so cancelled impurity seems to have no carrying impurity.

steps.title: A Possible Answer: It Is Rotted Impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests what רב דימי could have answered: the clump is different because it is 'rotted impurity.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is surely different here, because it is rotted impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why רב דימי stayed silent and offers an answer he could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clump of blood is decayed and spoiled, and rotted impurity does not make impure at all. If so, the clump case tells us nothing about cancelled impurity, and רב דימי's rule could still stand.

phrases.english: Perhaps: surely it is different here,
because it is rotted impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to אביי's challenge that רב דימי did not give.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the clump has a special reason it is pure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clump case proves cancelled impurity does not make impure by carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clump is pure because it is rotted impurity, not because of cancellation.

steps.title: Works for בר פדא, but What About רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The 'rotted impurity' answer fits בר פדא, who says severe impurity lasts only while fit for a גר. The גמרא begins to ask how it fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for בר פדא, who says: severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a גר, and light impurity until it is unfit for a dog. This clump is not fit for a גר. But according to רבי יוחנן, who says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the 'rotted impurity' answer works for everyone. It works for בר פדא, and now the גמרא sets up a question from רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בר פדא, severe impurity stops once the item is too spoiled for a גר to eat, and the clump is too spoiled for that, so it is pure. רבי יוחנן seems to hold a different measure, and his words come next, so the answer may not work for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a גר תושב: a non-Jew who keeps basic laws and may eat נבילה

phrases.english: This works well for Bar Padda, who says:
Severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a ger,
phrases.notes: גר here means a גר תושב, who is allowed to eat נבילה.

phrases.english: and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog,
and this clump is not fit for a ger.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'rotted impurity' answer against different opinions; sets up a challenge from רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer relies on בר פדא's measure of when impurity ends; רבי יוחנן may hold a different measure under which the clump would still be impure.
